reward_function.approach: Phase16 generic reward (displacement_weight * displacement + center_bonus - limit_penalty) with joint-type-specific limits and weights

completed_training.status: PARTIAL — Ep0 positive but training incomplete due to infra issues

lessons_learned.lesson: Phase16 generic reward (displacement * weight + center_bonus - limit_penalty) works across joint types when params are tuned per joint
lessons_learned.evidence: coxa_T1 (R=10.20), coxa_T1_right (R=11.31), coxa_abduct Ep0 (R=13.15 with limit=0.7, disp_w=6.0)
lessons_learned.impact: No need for complex multi-component reward — simple displacement + limit penalty suffices

lessons_learned.lesson: Narrow-ROM joints (abduct, twist) need LOWER displacement_weight to avoid limit-hitting oscillations
lessons_learned.evidence: coxa_abduct with disp_w=10.0 oscillates ±100pts; with disp_w=6.0 achieved stable R=+13.15 on Ep0
lessons_learned.impact: Use disp_w=4-6 for abduct/twist, 8-10 for coxa/femur/tibia

lessons_learned.lesson: Joint angle limit should match the wider end of the MuJoCo range plus margin
lessons_learned.evidence: coxa_abduct range [-1.0, 0.7], limit=0.7 works; limit=0.6 was too aggressive (R=-53)
lessons_learned.impact: Set limit = max(|lo|, |hi|) rounded up slightly

lessons_learned.lesson: Custom reward functions (v1, v2) with survival bonuses, Gaussian centering, and normalized displacement performed WORSE than the simple Phase16 formula
lessons_learned.evidence: v1/v2 rewards produced -23 to -338; Phase16 formula gave +7 to +20
lessons_learned.impact: KISS principle — simple displacement reward beats complex engineered rewards

lessons_learned.lesson: Training infrastructure needs improvement — output buffering, process management, and SSH reliability are bottlenecks
lessons_learned.evidence: Multiple training runs died silently; log files captured only Ep0; duplicate processes
lessons_learned.impact: Need: tmux/screen session, proper logging, or direct local execution

lessons_learned.lesson: The quick_train.py approach (Phase16 PerActuatorRL + joint-specific params) is the correct architecture
lessons_learned.evidence: Small, focused script that reuses proven PerActuatorRL with per-joint tuning
lessons_learned.impact: Use quick_train.py pattern for all 34 remaining actuators

next_steps: Fix training infrastructure (run directly on GB10 with tmux)
